selected.item: Cognition released SWE-2.1 on November 24, 2026, per its official blog (published 2026-11-24T08:00:00-08:00). Like its predecessor SWE-2, it is trained with pure reinforcement learning on Kimi K3. Cognition says it delivers large gains across coding benchmarks including FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.1 by targeting general intelligence and long-horizon workflows. On cybersecurity, SWE-2.1 achieves 80% on ExploitBench and captures 27.3% of flags via intended exploits on ExploitGym. Cognition also released SWE-2.1 Ultrafast through a Cerebras partnership, the same model at 10x the speed (600 tokens/s versus 60 tokens/s for standard SWE-2.1; SWE-2 Flash is 200 tokens/s), and SWE-2.1 Cyber, a version with more permissive safeguards, rolling out to Devin Security for defensive work. SWE-2.1 is available in Devin Desktop, Cloud and CLI; it is free through December 8, 2026 on Desktop and CLI, and at a discounted price until January 30. Secondary coverage of the announcement reports 50.0% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (up from 24.2 for SWE-2), 41.3% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 44.0% on ProgramBench; those figures are not in the fetched blog text, so this issue does not state them as blog-verified. All performance figures are Cognition's own measurements.
selected.note: The official blog carries a publication timestamp (2026-11-24T08:00:00-08:00). Terminal-Bench 4.1 50.0%, FrontierCode 2.0 41.3% and ProgramBench 44.0% are reported in secondary coverage of the same announcement, not in the fetched blog text, so they are recorded here as secondary-reported only.

selected.item: SenseTime released SenseNova U1.6 on November 24, 2026, an open-weight 8B native unified multimodal model for image generation and editing, per its official Hugging Face model card (sensenova/SenseNova-U1.6-8B-MoT) and the SenseNova-U1 GitHub repository. The BF16 checkpoint adds a native self-correction / interleaved protocol: the model draws an image, reads it back and fixes its own mistakes, including text errors in infographics. Weights are under Apache 2.0. The matching runtime is in the OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1 GitHub repository. A lighter U1.6 Lite is offered via the SenseNova Token Plan and apps, per secondary coverage. Performance figures are SenseTime's own claims, not independent verification.
selected.note: The Hugging Face model card itself carries no date line in the fetched text, and the repository was created 2026-11-16T17:00:53Z, so the November 24 date is recorded from announcement coverage dated November 24, 2026. License Apache 2.0 is stated on the model card.

selected.item: Tencent released OmniEVIE-4B on November 24, 2026, a 4.54B-parameter unified multimodal multi-vector retrieval model from Tencent IMA Product Center and Tencent Youtu Lab, per its official Hugging Face model card (repo created 2026-11-24T03:16:57Z). Built on Qwen3.5, it retrieves across text, natural images, visual documents and native video, and localizes each hit to a page region or video timestamp. Tencent reports it ranks #1 on the MMEB leaderboard excluding audio (60.68 full sequence, 60.06 compressed, across 190 tasks), and searches 1M records in 54.2 ms on a single CPU thread (120.2 ms for 5M). Weights and code are Apache 2.0, with the inference and indexing package on GitHub (Tencent/OmniEVIE). All benchmark figures are Tencent's own measurements.
selected.note: The model card itself carries no date line in the fetched text; the November 24 date is recorded from the Hugging Face API repository creation date (2026-11-24T03:16:57Z) and same-day announcement coverage. License Apache 2.0 is stated on the model card.

selected.item: Tencent open-sourced Hy-MT3 on November 24, 2026, the third generation of its Hunyuan multilingual translation model family, per the News line on its official Hugging Face model card ('2026.11.24 We open-sourced Hy-MT3-1.8B/Hy-MT3-7B/Hy-MT3-30B-A3B on HuggingFace and ModelScope, and released TransRubric on GitHub'). Three sizes are published: 1.8B, 7B and 30B-A3B (MoE, 3B active). Language coverage expands from 38 languages in Hy-MT2 to 102 languages. Versus Hy-MT2, Tencent reports mistranslations down 43%, omissions or additions down 74% and instruction-following errors down 40% on real-world scenario data. Hy-MT3-30B-A3B is tuned for game localization and OCR-cascaded image translation, and Tencent also open-sourced TransRubric, a rubric-based translation evaluation suite. All quality figures are Tencent's own measurements.
selected.note: The model card's News section states the release date November 24, 2026. License is reported as Apache 2.0 in secondary coverage; the fetched model-card text contains no license line, so the license is recorded as secondary-reported only.

selected.item: OpenAI released healthcare model configurations for the Responses API on November 24, 2026, per its official API changelog: gpt-6.2-astra-healthcare, gpt-6.2-sol-healthcare, gpt-6-astra-healthcare and gpt-6.1-sol-healthcare. These are configurations of the existing GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol models, not new base models: each pairs the base model with a harness tailored to clinical questions, and when the model uses web search it searches a dedicated index of medical sources. Prices match the base models per 1M tokens: $8 input / $40 output for gpt-6.2-astra-healthcare, $2 / $10 for gpt-6.2-sol-healthcare, $10 / $50 for gpt-6-astra-healthcare, and $2 / $10 for gpt-6.1-sol-healthcare. Promotional pricing for the healthcare configurations is available at least through December 31, 2026, per the pricing page.
selected.note: The changelog entry is dated November 24, 2026 (date only, no time). These are model configurations, not new base models; the distinction is stated in the article.
